newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kofi Annan leads in U N. vote but France may veto.
newsitem.headline: Kofi Annan leads in U N. vote but France may veto.

text.p: U.N. undersecretary-general Kofi Annan led the field in the first day of unofficial voting on Tuesday for the post of U.N. secretary-general, diplomats said.

Annan, in a second round of balloting in the Security Council, received 10 votes in favour with one negative vote, presumed to have come from France which has veto power. Annan, a native of Ghana, is in charge of U.N. peacekeeping.
The envoys said all four candidates received a negative vote from a veto-bearing permanent council member.
In second place was Ivory Coast's Foreign Minister Amara Essy, who received seven votes in favour while two permanent members opoposed him.

Hamid Algabid of Niger -- secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference -- received five votes in favour and two against from permanent members. Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah of Mauritania -- a former U.N. special envoy for Burundi who now heads the Washington-based Global Coalition for Africa -- received three votes in favour and two votes against from permanent members.

Each council member can vote for more than one nominee and no date was set for the first official vote. To win a candidate must have at least nine votes in favour and no veto from the United States, Britain, France, Russia or China.
